segments.line: You open your eyes in the hospital bed again.
The nurse doesn't look surprised this time. She looks scared.
Because the room is dark.
The whole hospital is dark.
Out the window, the whole city is dark.
And it's been a lot longer than four seconds.
The backup generators kick in.
The man in the suit is standing at the end of your bed.
'It didn't come back, ' he says quietly. 'Not this time. '
Your phone buzzes. A video from Mom.
Ellie, safe at home, holding a flashlight, waving at the camera.
And over her head, very faint, there's a little green bar.
So, is any of this real? The physics is.
A ten- story fall really ends at fifty- four miles an hour.
John Stapp really survived forty- six g.
And a car at thirty really needs six car lengths to stop.
And making a stop longer, like an airbag does, really is what keeps people safe every day.
Would you have made the dive? Tell me in the comments.
If you had the bar for just one day, what's the first thing you'd try?
And subscribe, because next time, we find out what happens when Ellie respawns.
